My Honest Review of Panda Animal Clinic

As a Google Local Guide, I take pride in providing honest, thorough reviews to help others make informed decisions. Unfortunately, my experience at Panda Animal Clinic left a lot to be desired, and I feel it’s important for pet owners to know what to expect before bringing their animals here.

The Pros:
Let’s start with the positive. The male veterinarian (appeared) to be kind, knowledgeable, and experienced, and is great and making people feel guilty. I have few complaints about his medical expertise or  demeanor—he seems to somewhat genuinely care about animals and knows what he’s talking about. The front desk staff is also very sweet, polite, and accommodating. I want to emphasize that the receptionists are doing their jobs well, and my issue is not with them at all.

The Cons:
Where this clinic really falls short is in how aggressively they try to upsell unnecessary services and products. While I understand that animal care can add up, I’ve been to enough veterinary clinics to know the difference between genuine recommendations and being pushed to spend more money. Here, the latter was the case. At every turn, it felt like I was being pressured into additional services, tests, or treatments that weren’t essential. This kind of behavior doesn’t sit well with me, especially when it feels exploitative of pet owners who just want the best care for their animals.

The experience took a sharp turn for the worse with the vet assistant, who was, to put it bluntly, extremely rude. She was a Cuban lady who became visibly frustrated when I didn’t understand Spanish. I respect everyone’s right to speak their preferred language, but work with me here not everyone speaks Spanish, and patients (or clients, in this case) should not be made to feel bad or uncomfortable for not understanding another language. Her attitude was unprofessional, condescending, and completely out of line for someone working in a customer-facing role at a clinic where clear communication is critical.

Overall Takeaway:
If you’re looking for a knowledgeable vet, you might find that here, but it comes at the cost of being pushed into spending money on things you don’t need. While the front desk staff are kind and the vet himself is somewhat competent, the clinic’s approach to customer service and their upselling practices are enough to turn me away for good. On top of that, the behavior of the assistant made the experience unnecessarily uncomfortable and unwelcoming.

It’s clear to me that this clinic has its priorities misaligned—focusing more on sales than providing a compassionate and stress-free experience for pet owners. I cannot recommend this place to others in good faith. If you care about transparency, professionalism, and fair treatment, I suggest you take your pets elsewhere.

RE:
1/20/25

Your reply only reinforces my concerns about the lack of accountability and professionalism at your clinic.

First, I understand the difference between genuine recommendations and upselling tactics, and unfortunately, my experience leaned heavily toward the latter. Simply claiming that your recommendations are based on pet needs does not address the pressure I felt to approve unnecessary services. If transparency and consent were truly a priority, the approach would have felt collaborative rather than transactional.

Second, regarding your technician: It’s disappointing to see her behavior excused with the explanation that she was “busy.” Being busy is not an excuse for unprofessionalism or making a client feel uncomfortable and unwelcome. The suggestion that I should have asked for someone who speaks English is troubling—it shouldn’t be my responsibility to ensure clear communication at a clinic operating in a diverse community. A professional should proactively ensure clients feel understood and respected, regardless of language barriers.

This response lacks accountability and instead deflects responsibility back onto the client. Unfortunately, it only reaffirms my decision to seek care for my pets elsewhere.

I spent over $900 on tests and X-rays, plus another $400 on food, probiotics, and supplements. After all that, I was told my dog might have an obstruction and would need an $850 ultrasound—yet they couldn’t even provide the service immediately because the necessary technician wasn’t available and would require a separate appointment.

Is this an emergency or not? I was given no clear guidance on what signs to watch for or when I should act urgently.
Following day, I called Panda because my dog wasn't doing any better, but due to the lack of guidance didn't know what to do or make of it, so they advised to find an emergency vet ultrasound, they also said they would send me some phone numbers. They never did.
I ended up going to another vet for clarity, only to find discrepancies in the records—like claims of blood in my dog’s urine, which apparently weren’t supported by the tests performed. It became obvious their focus wasn’t on my pet’s health but on selling overpriced food and supplements.

To make matters worse, I never received a single follow-up call to check on my dog’s condition. Their lack of care and communication is unacceptable. I won’t be going back
